St Paul's Infant School
EverybodyAchieving, Believing,SucceedingTogether
Our Values
At St Paul’s we have a core value for each term, these underpin everything that we do throughout the year:
Togetherness is a very important value to start the year. We encourage the children to make new friends and do things together to find out about each other’s interests.
Safety is the second value that we talk about at St Paul’s Infant School. Not just keeping yourself safe, but also how to keep others safe and we talk about staying safe online.
At St Paul’s we promote resilience in all of our children, whether it be in their academic learning or social experiences. Resilience plays a major part in getting our children to be independent learners.
Growth and change is all about how we have grown and developed throughout the year or during our time at school. We think back to times when we couldn’t do something and talk about how we have grown to be able to do it now. This value also comes along at the beginning of Spring, which means we get to talk about how the world around us is changing too.
Respect is an important life value and one that we like to encourage our children to adopt. The grownups at St Paul’s model respect for each other on a daily basis and encourage the children to do the same.
The value of aspiration is a great way to end the academic year. It teaches the children to reach for their goals and to dream big. Aspiration is a great word to teach our young children, it gets them to think about what they aspire to be and to listen to other peoples aspirations.

Wraparound Childcare
Wraparound Childcare
Early Start Club
Situated: St. Paul's Infant School
At St. Paul's our breakfast club is provided by our own staff. We do not offer an after school service currently. We provide an inviting and stimulating environment for children to feel relaxed before starting their school day. The breakfast club takes place in our school hall or in a classroom and starts from 8am. The children that attend the club either eat breakfast at home or bring their own breakfast items to eat at the club. All children can engage in various activities set up by the staff.
STARS @ NBJS
Situated: North Borough Junior School
Stars offers quality, affordable, wraparound childcare and is based within the school grounds at North Borough Junior School. It offers care before and after school. Children from the ages of 4-11 are catered for, providing a large range of activities including: sports and team games, art and craft, imaginative play, music and drama, manipulative play, cooking, outside play, books, puzzles, theme work, creative play, physical play, television and computer games. A quiet area is available, as well as an area to complete homework.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Pauls Infant School - Our Curriculum
pageCache.text:
Our Curriculum
Our Curriculum
Curriculum Intent
St Paul’s Infant School is founded on the values that have been created developed and embedded by the school community. These values of Togetherness, Safety, Resilience, Growth and change, Respect and Aspiration underpin all children’s whole school journey, including the curriculum and its delivery.
At St Paul’s we believe that creating a friendly, warm and welcoming environment where children are smiling, happy, feel safe and are keen to come to school is the way to help support and motivate them to become inquisitive, independent learners. St Paul’s also ensures that the children are supported by adults who understand them. Lessons are planned to enable all children to grow and develop. This encourages all children to show progress and move their own personal development forward. St Paul’s aims to equip all children with the knowledge and skills they need to succeed through life.
We believe that the children understand which subject they are learning and explore with them the distinctive features concerned with the subjects, as well as ensuring that the knowledge specific vocabulary is shared in these lessons. Our curriculum is constantly reviewed to consider the different experiences of the children. The adults in school also work hard to plan for opportunities to offer real life experiences which better support understanding. Our curriculum reflects the school’s local context by addressing typical gaps in children’s real life experiences including trips out of school as well as visitors into school. The planning and experiences encourage the children to develop a love of learning and a willingness to explore while having fun and gaining new knowledge.
The curriculum considers many different subject areas. Each of these are well led and monitored to ensure that at St Paul’s we are offering a well-balanced start to their learning journey. Our diverse curriculum connects subjects thereby giving a range of opportunities and a balance of knowledge and skills.
While learning outcomes are planned and progression is carefully considered, the children are offered the opportunity to access their learning in a variety of ways to suit them best. This delivery builds on the strong foundation of the child-initiated skills that the children acquire during their time in our Early
Years classrooms, it also encourages the children to continue with an independent investigation approach, which we feel is a skill for life.
As an infant school, we strongly believe in a positive start for the children working within the expectations of Development Matters for Early Years. This is where the children’s balanced curriculum journey begins. Our children will have the opportunity to be creative, to be physically active and to be academically challenged along each part of their school journey. In KS1, Science, History, Geography, DT and Art are connected by theme and mapped to the requirements of the National Curriculum. RE, RSE, Music, PE and Computing are taught as discrete subjects but where a relevant and meaningful link can be made to our connected units, this is done as well. (Parents/carers can withdraw their children from any/all RE lessons if they choose to, after discussion with Mrs Aldridge/Mrs Chiverton.)
At St Paul’s, our curriculum is reviewed yearly across the whole school community and adaptations are made to ensure that the children always continue to strive to be the best they can be.
If you have any further questions about our Curriculum please speak to our Curriculum Lead, Mrs Aldridge.

Phonics
At St Paul's, we follow a scheme called 'Read Write Inc.phonics' (RWI). This scheme ensures that our staff have the knowledge to teach every child to read, regardless of their age, background or need.
Read Write Inc. encourage staff to teach using a toy frog called 'Fred'. Fred can only 'speak' using his sounds. When sounding out words, children are taught to 'Fred Talk' the words using the sounds that they have been taught in phonics, rather than using the letter names. 'Fred Talk' may be a term that your child uses at home when decoding or spelling words.
The RWI programme allows children to move through different coloured groups as they learn more sounds. An outline of each group is described in the document linked below:
Click here to find out more about Read Write Inc. Phonics.
If you require any support or have any questions about phonics at St Paul's, our Phonics Leaders are Mrs Thomas and Mrs Davey; they will be happy to help where possible.

We are, together with North Borough, designing and decorating a 'Shaun the Sheep' sculpture to go in 'The Shaun the Sheep in the Heart of Kent' parade which is taking place all around Maidstone in 2024. The children have been very excited and have all had a go at designing a Shaun. There were some baaa-rilliant designs, and a design combining ideas from several children was chosen.
All of the staff and children across the federation have had a turn at painting a small section on the sheep. We have some 'sneak peeks' for you but can't reveal the whole design yet. Look out for our Shaun in the parade in Maidstone soon!

Learning Council
We value everyone’s voices at St Paul’s. One way in which we ensure that all voices are heard is through the Learning Council. The Learning Council is made up of 1 child from each class in the school with Miss Taylor and Mrs Clark. The learning council meet throughout the term to discuss a topic linked to our learning or our school in general. Once we have held a meeting, the representative from each class will take the next topic back to their class to gather their thoughts and ideas. The class feedback is then shared in our next meeting, where we discuss the level of priority or things that we can change and work on as a school.
Miss Taylor and Mrs Clark are the adults who run our learning council.

pageCache.pageTitle: St Pauls Infant School - Severe Weather Guidance
pageCache.text:
Severe Weather Guidance
Schools will stay open if at all possible when there is severe weather such as deep/drifting snow, very high winds or widespread flooding. Parents and carers have the responsibility of getting children/pupils to and from school safely and need to decide if the journey is safe when severe weather affects transport and/or walking conditions. Parents/carers should inform schools if their child is absent due to severe conditions making the journey unsafe. If your child has a disability and/or learning difficulty, your decision to take the journey must take this into consideration.
On occasions, schools will need to close, and a message will be sent to you via the Parentmail text/ e-mail system and on Class Dojo. You can go online to www.kentclosures.co.uk for information about school closures and information is also given out on BBC Radio Kent, Heart FM and KMFM Radio. If, on the rare occasion, school closes at a time within the school day, a message will be sent out via the Parentmail text/e-mail system and on Class Dojo. You can visit www.kent.gov.uk/winter for more information about gritting routes and travel issues around Kent.
Late opening and/or early closure is a possibility in poor weather conditions and schools will either inform parents the night before or via the Parentmail text/e-mail system, on Class Dojo or online at www.kentclosures.co.uk and on local radio.
If conditions worsen throughout the school day and parents feel it is absolutely necessary to collect children, the school should, if possible, be contacted prior to collection.
Please ensure your son/daughter is appropriately clothed for cold/wet/windy weather and that shoes/boots have good grip for icy conditions.

pageCache.text:
Month of the Military Child 2024
April was the month of the 'military child'. It is a time to recognise and celebrate the important role service children have within the military. Children of those serving in the military shared some of their experiences in their classrooms and in a whole school assembly.
Dandelions are the chosen flower of The Military Child. Dandelions are hardy plants which put down strong roots almost anywhere the wind carries them. Military children may bloom wherever the wind takes them. They can have strong roots, planted swiftly and surely. Each class at St Paul's created their own dandelion artwork to celebrate their service children peers. Have a look at some of the artwork below!
We are all so proud of the military children at our school and grateful for all they and their families do.
